title: Deviation read path is absent from the Ownership Map
source: Ownership Map v1 (api rows for S8 rwb-deviation); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15
description: rwb-case must read the deviations of one case to compose the case record answer, and the target names GET /api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations for it. Architecture v5 slide 15 gives rwb-deviation IN "GET/POST /deviations", but the Ownership Map lists only POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations and PATCH /deviations/{deviationId} for S8, so the read operation the app story consumes has no owner entry to contract, fake or test against.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15: "REST  GET/POST /deviations · POST /deviations/{id}/clear"; Ownership Map v1 api: "POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations" and "PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}", both owner S8, and no GET row.
proposed: Add GET /cases/{caseId}/deviations to the S8 rows of the Ownership Map and to the S8 API file; until then consume the read behind the S8 contract at that path with the 2 s timeout, as RWB-ITG-E2015-ITG already assumes.

title: No source gives the alert values for the timer projection, the degradation rate or the breach volume
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 28 and 44; legacy story RWB-E2-015 section 5
description: The deployment alerts on the timer projection lag, the MSG-GEN-006 degradation rate and TimerBreached volume, but no source gives a threshold, a window or a band. The legacy story names only a 2 s read timeout and a five-minute timer check that the target retires, and the FSD and TSD P3 give no operational value.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44: "JOB-21 Stuck workflow scan every 5 min, platform, visibility query + alert"; slide 28: "Stops at once (no retry); stuck-case alert"; no threshold appears in FSD P3 v4, TSD P3 v3 or RWB-E2-015.
proposed: Set the three values in the rwb-case values files, confirm them at UAT and record the agreed values in the runbook entry each alert links.

title: Case interaction-ledger read has no agreed owner-side contract path
source: _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (api 'GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions' owner P1; tables 'interaction' ruling ASM-A6-tables-1); TSD P3 v3 appendix T-A.1 API-P3-014; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-18
section: s12.2 REST operations consumed; s11 Data
description: RWB-E2-016 puts the contacts of a case on the timeline. The table ruling keeps the case timeline and interaction API with rwb-case, the API map gives the two interaction operations to rwb-source-data and states no read path on the P1 base, and TSD P3 v3 records them as API-P3-014 and API-P3-015 in P3. The app story therefore cannot name the operation it calls for the eight contact items of AC1 or the masking of their summaries.
evidence: ownership.json interaction.ruling: 'the case timeline and interaction API stay with P3 ... integration reads the ledger through P1's contract'; ownership.json api 'GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions': owner P1; the map lists no P1 base path or response shape for that read; TSD P3 v3 API-P3-014.
proposed: Publish one case-scoped interaction-ledger read on the rwb-source-data base with the query and the masked summary shape of API-P3-014, and record in the Ownership Map which interaction operation rwb-case keeps.

title: Case-scoped notice list has no Ownership Map row
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17 (rwb-comms IN: GET /cases/{id}/notices); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json api section
description: The timeline needs the notices of a case. Architecture v5 slide 17 gives rwb-comms a case-scoped notice list, but the Ownership Map API section has only GET /notices/{noticeId} and POST /cases/{caseId}/notices, so the operation the timeline consumes has no map row, no confirmed response shape and no stated rights.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 17 rwb-comms IN: 'POST /notices (request) · GET /cases/{id}/notices'; ownership.json api has 'GET /notices/{noticeId}' and 'POST /cases/{caseId}/notices' and no case-scoped notice list.
proposed: Add the case-scoped notice list to the Ownership Map API section under P6 with its query and response shape, and align the P6 contract baseline to it.

title: The case-side rule-change audit read has no row in the ownership map
source: Ownership Map v1 (_work/msr/plan/ownership.json); API Specification v4; legacy RWB-E2-041 section 12; FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.16
section: 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.7 Tables owned; section 16
description: RWB-E2-041 owns the change report and the decisions per package version, but in the target only the P7 report is mapped. No source gives a case-side audit operation, so its owner, path, security right, entry fields, CSV column order and size limits had to be chosen: owner rwb-case, GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/rule-change-audit, Rules and parameters R, one entry per package version with decisions, casesAffected, firstDecisionAt, lastDecisionAt, openCasesAtVersion and openCasesKeepingVersion.
evidence: ownership.json maps GET /queues/{queueId}/cases and GET /cases/{caseId} to P3 and GET /admin/rule-packages/change-report to P7; no case-side audit path appears in the api block or in TSD v5 P3 appendix T-A. The legacy section 12 gives one monolith path only.
proposed: Publish GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/rule-change-audit in the rwb-case API file with the entry fields of section 11 and Rules and parameters R, and add the row to the ownership map before the wave 2 contract baseline is tagged.

title: FSD A2.16 reports reference-data changes while the legacy story and the test cases govern rule package versions
source: FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.16 (AC-P3-016-01, AC-ALT-P3-016-01); legacy RWB-E2-041 sections 1 to 17; WP B-P3-04 story line
section: Section 1 scope; section 19 out of scope
description: The functional specification illustrates the change checklist and the report with SERVICE_LEVEL version 4, status VALIDATED and a reference-data service, while the legacy acceptance criteria, the test cases and the WP title are rule package versions with LOADED, APPROVED and IN_FORCE. §R3 puts the functional specification above the story masters, so the two cannot both be copied. This story keeps the rule package scope because the title, the legacy key and all eleven legacy test cases are rule packages, and the reference-data checklist keeps its own story RWB-E1-043.
evidence: FSD A2.16 AC-P3-016-01 uses table SERVICE_LEVEL version 4 loaded by U-REF-01 and AC-ALT-P3-016-01 shows status VALIDATED; legacy AC1 to AC10 use ALLOCATION 'ALLOC-2026.12' and status LOADED.
proposed: Record the rule-package scope for RWB-E2-041 and keep the reference-data checklist and its report with RWB-E1-043; revisit if the FSD example is the intended target.

title: Retention and lifecycle windows of the new audit read and its contract are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 28 and 29; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T2.2; WP B-P3-04
section: Section 3 preconditions; section 13 configuration; section 19 out of scope
description: No source fixes how long the case-side audit answer or its CSV export is kept, how long a published field stays before it may be removed, or how long the contract fakes are retained. The answer is computed per request from rows the service already holds, so its retention follows the decision records it summarises; the other two windows stay open.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 29 fixes schema, login and migration ownership only; TSD P3 T2.2 fixes the package version pin and writes no retention; the legacy story sets none.
proposed: Set the audit read retention against the decision-record retention and state a deprecation window for a published field in the contract README.

title: The rule package registry is declared in the P3 module and owned by P7
source: TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 (T2.1 RulePackageRepository, T2.2 Rules package, T3.1 rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case); TSD P4 v3 T3.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 27 and 41; Ownership Map v1 (rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case; ruling ASM-A6-tables-3); legacy RWB-E2-042 sections 3, 4, 11 and 13
section: s7 Acceptance criteria; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s13 Solution plan; s19 Out of scope
description: TSD P3 v3 declares the four registry tables and a RulePackageRepository inside the case module, and the legacy story loads, approves and asserts rule_row through P3. The ownership ruling and Arch v5 put the registry, the rule rows, the test cases and the admin operations in rwb-decision. The legacy AC1 to AC3 therefore assert facts this P3 story does not own: the story proves them against the rwb-decision contract mock and carries the registry work, the seeding and JOB-20 to RWB-P7-E2042-APP, with the real cross-service proof in RWB-ITG-E2042-ITG.
evidence: TSD P3 v3 T2.1 'RulePackageRepository reads rule_package, rule_package_version and rule_row'; T3.1 headings 'rule_package (NEW, owned by P4)' and 'rule_row additions (table owned by P4)'; Ownership Map rule_row, rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_test_case owner P7 with ruling ASM-A6-tables-3; Arch v5 slide 41 P7 'approvals, central decision ledger, DMN model registry'.
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the P3 tech lead
proposed: Keep the registry, the seeding, the admin operations, the approval, the rollback and JOB-20 in RWB-P7-E2042-APP (ASM-A6-tables-3); keep the workbooks, the model cache, the checksum check, the atomic swap, the catalog read and the schema assertion in RWB-P3-E2042-APP; prove AC1 to AC3 against the rwb-decision contract mock here and against the real service in RWB-ITG-E2042-ITG.

title: The rule-model and rule-catalog read operations have no published field-level shape
source: Ownership Map v1 api section; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T2.2 (RuleResult, RuleCatalog.row); Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 15 and 16; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 27
section: s11 Data; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13 Build steps
description: Every consuming story calls GET /rule-models/{packageCode}/{version} and GET /rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion=, but neither appears in the Ownership Map API list, and no read source fixes the response elements, the error codes or the compiler-version element of the model. This key fixes the element names and fakes the shapes on Day 1; the property types, lengths and required flags stay open for the rwb-decision owner.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 lists only the six /admin/rule-* operations, all with x_module P7; TSD P3 v3 T2.2 gives the Java signatures RuleResult and RuleRow but no wire shape; Temporal and Drools slide 15 names 'GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}' and 'verifies the checksum' without a payload; Arch v5 slide 27 names the same call.
proposed: Publish the model and catalog resources in the rwb-decision contract with packageCode, versionLabel, checksum (SHA-256), model content and compiler version, valid-from date, and ruleId, packageVersion, drools_rule_name, action_text, owner_role, timer_spec, target_queue_code and outputs; until then the RWB-P3-E2042-CON baseline and its WireMock fake carry the assumed shapes.

title: Blob immutability period, pod memory for 20 KieBases, alert windows and probe timings are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E2-042 preconditions and section 13 (Blob paths, write-once, checksum in metadata); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 27 (cache, under 300 ms); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 16 (LRU max 20)
section: s11 Data; s13 Solution plan; s17 Guardrails (INF and OPS stories of this key)
description: The legacy story says only that the container exists and that the module identity has write and read rights on it. No source states the retention or immutability period of the container, the heap a pod needs to hold 20 KieBases of the three packages, the alert windows, the replica counts or the probe timings. RWB-P3-E2042-INF and RWB-P3-E2042-OPS expose them as reviewed values per environment and record them as assumptions rather than as business values.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-042 states 'The Blob container rule-packages exists and the recovery module identity has write and read rights on that container only'; Arch v5 slide 27 gives the 300 ms evaluation target and the cache but no memory figure; Temporal and Drools slide 16 gives 'KieBaseRegistry holds one KieBase per package version (LRU, max 20)' and no sizing.
owner_role: SCB IT infrastructure with the DevOps team
proposed: Set the container to write-once with no deletion and the reviewed audit retention per environment, size the pod by a load test that caches 20 versions, and expose the alert windows, replica counts and probe timings as reviewed values files; confirm all three with the platform and audit owners before the wave 2 release.

title: Reference fixture lifecycle, store and owner for the synthetic case
source: RWB-E2-043 section 3 and section 11; RWB-P3-E2043-APP section 3, 11, 13; RWB-P3-E2043-OPS section 11
description: The synthetic case RW-2026-000777 is named as a precondition, but no source states which store holds the fixture, who seeds it, which environments receive it, or who removes it after the test. The app story assumes a harness-owned JSON seed in the test resources of DEV and SIT; that choice is not backed by a document.
evidence: RWB-E2-043: 'The synthetic case "RW-2026-000777" exists in the DEV and SIT test data and is marked synthetic'; 'The fixture row is inserted by the test harness in DEV and SIT only and removed after the test' - no seed artefact, store, owner role or removal step is given.
proposed: Keep the fixture as a JSON seed under the test resources, owned by the app story, loaded and removed per run in DEV and SIT only, and carried by no release.

title: Worker build ID format and worker versioning policy are not stated
source: Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 27; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T2.4 and T2.5; RWB-P3-E2043-APP section 12.5 and 13; RWB-P3-E2043-OPS section 12.5 and 13
description: The design requires worker versioning and a build ID per worker, and the TSD names a WorkerBuildIdProvider, but no source fixes the build ID format, whether builds are pinned or auto-upgraded, the drain time of an old build, or which role sets the policy. The three stories state the rule and leave the values to the platform.
evidence: Design slide 27 notes: 'Worker Versioning (workers pinned to a build; needs Temporal 1.30+)'; TSD P3 T2.1 lists WorkerBuildIdProvider 'Supplies the build ID of the running worker to the replay gate'; no format or policy value appears in either.
proposed: Fix the build ID as the release commit ID supplied by the workflow kit, pin builds with drain-on-complete, and let the platform workflow kit owner set the policy once for all 19 services.

title: Replay corpus, history retention and the text of MSG-P3-038
source: Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 27; RWB-P3-E2043-CON section 12.5 and 14; RWB-P3-E2043-OPS section 13 and 14
section: 12.5 Workflows and activities; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: The replay gate is required on every build, but no source states how many recorded histories the gate replays, which environment they come from, how long they are kept, or the agreed wording of the replay-gate message. The stories state the gate, the report fields and the block on promotion, and leave the corpus and the message text open.
evidence: Design slide 27 notes: 'the replay gate (E2-040, MSG-P3-038) that replays recorded histories against every new build before release' - the corpus, its retention and the message text are not given anywhere in the extracts read.
proposed: Replay one recorded history per acceptance path of the reference fixture, keep them with the contract jar, and take the MSG-P3-038 text from the message catalogue before the gate is made mandatory in the pipeline.

title: Field-level detail of RecordAndApplyRequest and of the rule outputs map
source: RWB-E2-043 section 12 and 13; RWB-P3-E2043-CON section 11 and 12.5
description: The contract fixes the field names of the request record and the four members of RuleResult, but no source states the types, cardinality, required flags, or which rule output is mandatory for a given package. The detail is left to the baseline review of the contract story.
evidence: RWB-E2-043 section 12 declares 'RuleResult(String packageCode, String packageVersion, String ruleId, Map<String,Object> outputs)' and 'ApplyStateActivity.apply(CaseStateChange change, String idempotencyKey)' without field-level detail; the TSD P3 T2.2 publishes the same shape only.
proposed: Settle the request record and the outputs map at the baseline review, with the event key, the rule result, the state change and the business date as the only request members and a package-specific output schema.
